levels: No position held. The business HOLDS nothing a buyer could prefer: it competes on price or availability, or the claim exists only on paper -- a plan, a pitch, or an intention. No buyer currently chooses it for anything. AN UNCLAIMED GAP IN THE MARKET IS NOT A POSITION: spotting white space is not holding it, and openness is recorded separately in competitive_room. If nobody has been displaced and no buyer chooses this business for the claim, score 1.
Not held. A real claim, but one a named occupant already owns, or so generic that everyone in the category makes it. Buyers comparing would find no reason to prefer it.

Held, but not distinctive. The business holds a real claim -- it can point to a product, a method or a delivery it actually has, not merely one it intends -- but several occupants also make it or could match it easily. A place held, not an advantage: a rival could say the same thing tomorrow without changing anything.

Held and distinct. The business holds a claim the named occupants do NOT own, and buyers would prefer it for that specific thing -- a genuine flank it can win on, demonstrated rather than asserted. Proven against a named rival; a merely unclaimed gap is not this.

Dominant. The reference occupant of its situation -- rivals are defined AGAINST it, or its claim is the one others copy. A business that IS the default answer for what it sells holds this, and its prevalence is the evidence, not a fault. Dominance in a narrow situation counts; it does not require fame or scale.
added: THE HELD-vs-UNCLAIMED TEST, APPLIED BEFORE CHOOSING A LEVEL: a position must be something the business ALREADY HOLDS, evidenced by what it does or has -- a product it makes, a method it runs, a delivery it performs. A claim that exists only in a plan, and has displaced no occupant, scores 1 or 2 and NEVER 3 or 4. This matters because openness of the market is scored by competitive_room and market_headroom, not here: do NOT re-award an unclaimed space as a held position. ⚠ DO NOT CONFUSE HOLDING A POSITION WITH PROVING THE ROUTE TO SCALE. Whether the business can REACH buyers in volume -- distribution, outlets, channel, the cost of acquiring a customer -- is DEMAND REACH, scored separately. A business with a real, differentiated product it already makes and sells, but an unproven route to a mass market, HOLDS its position: score 3 or 4 on that alone. Judge whether the thing it offers is REAL AND ITS OWN, never how many buyers it has reached or could reach.
